whyItMatters: Unbounded copy functions write past the destination when input is overlong, corrupting adjacent memory — the classic buffer overflow.
actions: Switch to bounded variants with the real destination size (strncpy, strncat, snprintf).
Replace gets() with fgets() unconditionally — gets() has no safe use.
Prove every remaining copy fits: destination size must dominate the longest possible input.
verification: No unbounded copy call remains; gets() is gone entirely.

example.caveat: sizeof works on arrays, not on decayed pointers — track heap sizes explicitly.
